subject: maths
title: Year 6 Ratio and Proportion
seo_title: Year 6 Ratio and Proportion Worksheets: Scaling, Scale Factors and Sharing in a Ratio (Free, with Answers)
standard_text: Solve problems involving the relative sizes of two quantities where missing values can be found by using integer multiplication and division facts; solve problems involving similar shapes where the scale factor is known or can be found; solve problems involving unequal sharing and grouping using knowledge of fractions and multiples.
meta_desc: Free Year 6 ratio and proportion worksheets for the National Curriculum: write ratios as a : b, link ratios and fractions, scale recipes, use scale factors with similar shapes, share in a ratio with bar models and solve SATs-style problems. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Ratio 2 : 3 means 2 + 3 = 5 equal parts. Find one part, then multiply.
key_sub: Share £60 in the ratio 2 : 3: £60 ÷ 5 = £12, so £24 and £36. Red : blue = 3 : 2 means 3/5 are red. In proportion and enlargements, multiply or divide — never add.
body_html:
What is a ratio?

A ratio compares one amount with another. We write it with a colon: a : b. We say it with “for every … there are …”.

Order matters. Circles to squares is 1 : 2. Squares to circles is 2 : 1.

To simplify a ratio, divide both numbers by the same number, just like a fraction.

Ratio and fractions

Add the numbers in the ratio to find the whole. If red : blue = 3 : 2, every group has 3 + 2 = 5 counters, so 35 of the counters are red and 25 are blue.

Ratio red : blueRed as a fraction of allBlue as a fraction of all
3 : 23525
1 : 41545
5 : 35838

Proportion: scaling up and down

When amounts are in proportion, you multiply or divide them all by the same number. You never add.

Example

A recipe for 4 people needs 300 g of flour. How much flour is needed for 6 people?

Find 1 person first: 300 ÷ 4 = 75 g. Then 6 people: 75 × 6 = 450 g.

Answer: 450 g

Scale factors and similar shapes

An enlargement multiplies every length by the same scale factor. The new shape is similar: the same shape, a different size. The angles do not change.

Example

Find the scale factor from a 4 cm side to a 20 cm side.

Divide the new length by the old length: 20 ÷ 4 = 5.

Answer: scale factor 5

Sharing in a ratio

Draw a bar model with one box for each part. Every box is worth the same.

Example

Amelia and Jack share £60 in the ratio 2 : 3. How much does each get?

2 + 3 = 5 equal parts. £60 ÷ 5 = £12 in each part. Amelia: 2 × £12 = £24. Jack: 3 × £12 = £36.

Answer: Amelia £24, Jack £36

“3 times as many boys as girls” means boys : girls = 3 : 1. That is 4 parts, not 3.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Writing red : blue = 3 : 2 as the fraction 32 or 23Add the parts to find the whole: red is 35 of all
Adding instead of multiplying: 3 cm enlarged by scale factor 3 is 6 cmMultiply: 3 cm × 3 = 9 cm
Sharing £60 in 2 : 3 by working out £60 ÷ 2 and £60 ÷ 3Add the parts first: 2 + 3 = 5, so one part is £60 ÷ 5 = £12
Writing the ratio the wrong way roundThe first thing named goes first: boys to girls is boys : girls
“3 times as many” shared into 3 parts3 times as many is 3 : 1, which is 3 + 1 = 4 parts

faq.q: What is ratio and proportion in Year 6?
faq.a: Year 6 is the first year that ratio appears in the National Curriculum. Children use the a : b notation, scale recipes up and down, use scale factors with similar shapes and share amounts in a given ratio.

faq.q: How do you share an amount in a ratio?
faq.a: Add the numbers in the ratio to find the number of equal parts, divide the amount by that number, then multiply. For £60 in the ratio 2 : 3: 60 ÷ 5 = 12, so the shares are £24 and £36.
A scale factor tells you how many times bigger an enlarged shape is. Every length is multiplied by it, so a 3 cm by 5 cm rectangle enlarged by scale factor 3 becomes 9 cm by 15 cm.

faq.q: Is ratio tested in the Year 6 SATs?
faq.a: Yes. Ratio and proportion is part of the Year 6 curriculum, so it can come up in the KS2 SATs, usually as word problems in the reasoning papers (Papers 2 and 3), such as recipes, maps and sharing.

sets.title: Ratios from pictures, and ratio as a fraction

items.q: In a box, 14 of the chocolates are milk chocolates. The rest are dark chocolates. What is the ratio of milk chocolates to dark chocolates?
items.e: 14 means 1 out of every 4. The rest is 4 − 1 = 3 out of every 4. So milk chocolates : dark chocolates = 1 : 3, not 1 : 4.

items.q: Which sentence is true for this picture?
c: For every 3 circles there are 2 squares.
For every 2 circles there are 3 squares.
For every 3 circles there are 5 squares.
For every 6 circles there are 2 squares.
items.e: There are 6 circles and 4 squares, so circles : squares = 6 : 4. Divide both by 2: 3 : 2. So for every 3 circles there are 2 squares.

items.q: In a car park, the ratio of cars to vans is 4 : 5. What fraction of the vehicles are vans?
items.e: For every 4 cars there are 5 vans, so each group has 4 + 5 = 9 vehicles. 5 of every 9 are vans: 59. 54 is the wrong fraction: the denominator must be the whole group, 9.

items.q: In a bag, the ratio of red counters to blue counters is 5 : 3. What fraction of the counters are blue?
items.e: For every 5 red counters there are 3 blue counters, so each group has 5 + 3 = 8 counters. 3 of every 8 are blue counters: 38. 35 is the wrong fraction: the denominator must be the whole group, 8.

items.q: In a choir, 47 of the children are girls. The rest are boys. What is the ratio of girls to boys?
items.e: 47 means 4 out of every 7. The rest is 7 − 4 = 3 out of every 7. So girls : boys = 4 : 3, not 4 : 7.

items.q: What fraction of the shapes are circles?
items.e: There are 6 + 3 = 9 shapes. 6 of them are circles, so 69 of the shapes are circles. 63 compares circles with squares, not with all the shapes.

items.q: In a bowl, the ratio of apples to pears is 3 : 4. What fraction of the pieces of fruit are apples?
items.e: For every 3 apples there are 4 pears, so each group has 3 + 4 = 7 pieces of fruit. 3 of every 7 are apples: 37. 34 is the wrong fraction: the denominator must be the whole group, 7.

items.q: What is the ratio of circles to squares?
items.e: Count: 2 circles and 5 squares. Circles are named first, so write 2 first: 2 : 5. 5 : 2 would be squares to circles.

items.q: What is the ratio of squares to circles?
items.e: Count: 4 squares and 7 circles. Squares are named first, so write 4 first: 4 : 7. 7 : 4 would be circles to squares.

items.q: What is the ratio of squares to circles?
items.e: Count: 8 squares and 2 circles. Squares are named first, so write 8 first: 8 : 2. 2 : 8 would be circles to squares.

items.q: Which sentence is true for this picture?
c: For every 6 circles there is 1 square.
For every 2 circles there are 3 squares.
For every 2 circles there is 1 square.
For every 1 circle there are 2 squares.
items.e: There are 6 circles and 3 squares, so circles : squares = 6 : 3. Divide both by 3: 2 : 1. So for every 2 circles there is 1 square.

items.q: Which sentence is true for this picture?
c: For every 4 circles there is 1 square.
For every 8 circles there is 1 square.
For every 4 circles there are 5 squares.
For every 1 circle there are 4 squares.
items.e: There are 8 circles and 2 squares, so circles : squares = 8 : 2. Divide both by 2: 4 : 1. So for every 4 circles there is 1 square.

items.q: What is the ratio of circles to squares?
items.e: Count: 6 circles and 7 squares. Circles are named first, so write 6 first: 6 : 7. 7 : 6 would be squares to circles.

items.q: In a flower bed, the ratio of tulips to daffodils is 2 : 3. What fraction of the flowers are tulips?
items.e: For every 2 tulips there are 3 daffodils, so each group has 2 + 3 = 5 flowers. 2 of every 5 are tulips: 25. 23 is the wrong fraction: the denominator must be the whole group, 5.

items.q: What fraction of the shapes are circles?
items.e: There are 2 + 6 = 8 shapes. 2 of them are circles, so 28 of the shapes are circles. 26 compares circles with squares, not with all the shapes.

items.q: What fraction of the shapes are squares?
items.e: There are 7 + 3 = 10 shapes. 3 of them are squares, so 310 of the shapes are squares. 37 compares squares with circles, not with all the shapes.

items.q: In an animal rescue centre, the ratio of cats to dogs is 6 : 5. What fraction of the animals are cats?
items.e: For every 6 cats there are 5 dogs, so each group has 6 + 5 = 11 animals. 6 of every 11 are cats: 611. 65 is the wrong fraction: the denominator must be the whole group, 11.

items.q: What is the ratio of circles to squares?
items.e: Count: 5 circles and 4 squares. Circles are named first, so write 5 first: 5 : 4. 4 : 5 would be squares to circles.

items.q: What is the ratio of circles to squares?
items.e: Count: 5 circles and 7 squares. Circles are named first, so write 5 first: 5 : 7. 7 : 5 would be squares to circles.

items.q: In a class library, 13 of the books are fiction books. The rest are non-fiction books. What is the ratio of fiction books to non-fiction books?
items.e: 13 means 1 out of every 3. The rest is 3 − 1 = 2 out of every 3. So fiction books : non-fiction books = 1 : 2, not 1 : 3.

sets.title: Scaling recipes and finding missing values

items.q: Find the missing number. 6 : 7 = 48 : ☐
items.e: 6 × 8 = 48, so multiply the second number by 8 too: 7 × 8 = 56. Adding 42 to both numbers (49) does not keep the ratio.

items.q: In a garden, for every 3 roses there are 5 tulips. There are 20 tulips. How many roses are there?
items.e: 20 tulips is 4 groups of 5 (20 ÷ 5 = 4). Each group has 3 roses: 4 × 3 = 12 roses.

items.q: Find the missing number. 7 : 5 = 35 : ☐
items.e: 7 × 5 = 35, so multiply the second number by 5 too: 5 × 5 = 25. Adding 28 to both numbers (33) does not keep the ratio.

items.q: 3 bread rolls cost £1.35. How much do 7 bread rolls cost?
Find the missing number. 4 : 7 = ☐ : 56
items.e: 7 × 8 = 56, so multiply the first number by 8 too: 4 × 8 = 32. Adding 49 to both numbers (53) does not keep the ratio.

items.q: A recipe for pancakes for 4 people uses 300 g of flour. How much flour is needed for 6 people?
items.e: For 1 person: 300 ÷ 4 = 75 g. For 6 people: 75 × 6 = 450 g.

items.q: Write 28 : 16 in its simplest form.
items.e: 4 is the highest common factor of 28 and 16. Divide both numbers by 4: 28 ÷ 4 = 7 and 16 ÷ 4 = 4, so the answer is 7 : 4.

items.q: In a pot, for every 4 pencils there are 7 pens. There are 28 pens. How many pencils are there?
items.e: 28 pens is 4 groups of 7 (28 ÷ 7 = 4). Each group has 4 pencils: 4 × 4 = 16 pencils.

items.q: A recipe for vegetable soup for 4 people uses 600 ml of stock. How much stock is needed for 10 people?
items.e: For 1 person: 600 ÷ 4 = 150 ml. For 10 people: 150 × 10 = 1,500 ml.

items.q: Find the missing number. 3 : 2 = ☐ : 14
items.e: 2 × 7 = 14, so multiply the first number by 7 too: 3 × 7 = 21. Adding 12 to both numbers (15) does not keep the ratio.

items.q: Write 20 : 12 in its simplest form.
items.e: 4 is the highest common factor of 20 and 12. Divide both numbers by 4: 20 ÷ 4 = 5 and 12 ÷ 4 = 3, so the answer is 5 : 3.

items.q: Write 8 : 12 in its simplest form.
items.e: 4 is the highest common factor of 8 and 12. Divide both numbers by 4: 8 ÷ 4 = 2 and 12 ÷ 4 = 3, so the answer is 2 : 3.

items.q: A recipe for pizza dough for 8 people uses 480 g of flour. How much flour is needed for 2 people?
items.e: For 1 person: 480 ÷ 8 = 60 g. For 2 people: 60 × 2 = 120 g. Fewer people need less, so the answer must be smaller than 480 g.

items.q: 4 apples cost 80p. How much do 10 apples cost?
A recipe for shortbread for 6 people uses 120 g of butter. How much butter is needed for 15 people?
items.e: For 1 person: 120 ÷ 6 = 20 g. For 15 people: 20 × 15 = 300 g.

items.q: A recipe for a fruit smoothie for 2 people uses 250 ml of milk. How much milk is needed for 5 people?
items.e: For 1 person: 250 ÷ 2 = 125 ml. For 5 people: 125 × 5 = 625 ml.

items.q: 6 cupcakes cost £4.20. How much do 9 cupcakes cost?
On a school trip, for every 2 adults there are 15 children. There are 6 adults. How many children are there?
items.e: 6 adults is 3 groups of 2 (6 ÷ 2 = 3). Each group has 15 children: 3 × 15 = 45 children.

items.q: 5 pencils cost £1.50. How much do 8 pencils cost?
A recipe for apple crumble for 6 people uses 180 g of flour. How much flour is needed for 9 people?
items.e: For 1 person: 180 ÷ 6 = 30 g. For 9 people: 30 × 9 = 270 g.

items.q: A photo is 12 cm wide and 18 cm tall. A smaller copy is made with the same shape. The copy is 4 cm wide. How tall is the copy?
items.e: 12 ÷ 4 = 3, so every length of the copy is the original length divided by 3. Height: 18 ÷ 3 = 6 cm. Taking away 8 cm (18 − 8) does not keep the same shape.

items.q: The two triangles are similar. What is the missing length?
items.e: Scale factor: 9 ÷ 3 = 3. Missing length: 5 × 3 = 15 cm. Adding 6 cm (11 cm) does not keep the shape the same.

items.q: A poster is 25 cm wide and 30 cm tall. A smaller copy is made with the same shape. The copy is 5 cm wide. How tall is the copy?
items.e: 25 ÷ 5 = 5, so every length of the copy is the original length divided by 5. Height: 30 ÷ 5 = 6 cm. Taking away 20 cm (30 − 20) does not keep the same shape.

items.q: The two rectangles are similar. What is the missing length?
items.e: Scale factor: 15 ÷ 5 = 3. Missing length: 2 × 3 = 6 cm. Adding 10 cm (12 cm) does not keep the shape the same.

items.q: A painting is 16 cm wide and 24 cm tall. A smaller copy is made with the same shape. The copy is 4 cm wide. How tall is the copy?
items.e: 16 ÷ 4 = 4, so every length of the copy is the original length divided by 4. Height: 24 ÷ 4 = 6 cm. Taking away 12 cm (24 − 12) does not keep the same shape.

items.q: Rectangle A is 5 cm by 3 cm. It is enlarged by scale factor 5 to make rectangle B. What size is rectangle B?
items.e: Multiply every length by 5: 5 × 5 = 25 and 3 × 5 = 15. B is 25 cm by 15 cm. Adding 5 (10 cm by 8 cm) is not an enlargement.

items.q: Rectangle A is 3 cm by 5 cm. It is enlarged by scale factor 3 to make rectangle B. What size is rectangle B?
items.e: Multiply every length by 3: 3 × 3 = 9 and 5 × 3 = 15. B is 9 cm by 15 cm. Adding 3 (6 cm by 8 cm) is not an enlargement.

items.q: Triangle B is an enlargement of triangle A. What is the scale factor?
items.e: Compare matching sides: 12 ÷ 4 = 3 and 9 ÷ 3 = 3. Each side is 3 times as long, so the scale factor is 3. The difference (12 − 4 = 8) is not the scale factor.

items.q: Which rectangle is an enlargement of a rectangle 2 cm by 3 cm?
items.e: In an enlargement both sides are multiplied by the same number. 2 × 3 = 6 and 3 × 3 = 9, so 6 cm by 9 cm is an enlargement with scale factor 3.

items.q: The two rectangles are similar. What is the missing length?
items.e: Scale factor: 12 ÷ 3 = 4. Missing length: 2 × 4 = 8 cm. Adding 9 cm (11 cm) does not keep the shape the same.

items.q: Rectangle B is an enlargement of rectangle A. What is the scale factor?
items.e: Compare matching sides: 6 ÷ 2 = 3 and 9 ÷ 3 = 3. Each side is 3 times as long, so the scale factor is 3. The difference (6 − 2 = 4) is not the scale factor.

items.q: Rectangle B is an enlargement of rectangle A. What is the scale factor?
items.e: Compare matching sides: 8 ÷ 2 = 4 and 20 ÷ 5 = 4. Each side is 4 times as long, so the scale factor is 4. The difference (8 − 2 = 6) is not the scale factor.

items.q: The two rectangles are similar. What is the missing length?
items.e: Scale factor: 6 ÷ 3 = 2. Missing length: 4 × 2 = 8 cm. Adding 3 cm (7 cm) does not keep the shape the same.

items.q: Rectangle A is 4 cm by 6 cm. It is enlarged by scale factor 2 to make rectangle B. What size is rectangle B?
items.e: Multiply every length by 2: 4 × 2 = 8 and 6 × 2 = 12. B is 8 cm by 12 cm. Adding 2 (6 cm by 8 cm) is not an enlargement.

items.q: Which rectangle is an enlargement of a rectangle 2 cm by 5 cm?
items.e: In an enlargement both sides are multiplied by the same number. 2 × 4 = 8 and 5 × 4 = 20, so 8 cm by 20 cm is an enlargement with scale factor 4.

items.q: The two triangles are similar. What is the missing length?
items.e: Scale factor: 15 ÷ 5 = 3. Missing length: 2 × 3 = 6 cm. Adding 10 cm (12 cm) does not keep the shape the same.

items.q: Which rectangle is an enlargement of a rectangle 3 cm by 4 cm?
items.e: In an enlargement both sides are multiplied by the same number. 3 × 2 = 6 and 4 × 2 = 8, so 6 cm by 8 cm is an enlargement with scale factor 2.

items.q: Rectangle A is 2 cm by 7 cm. It is enlarged by scale factor 4 to make rectangle B. What size is rectangle B?
items.e: Multiply every length by 4: 2 × 4 = 8 and 7 × 4 = 28. B is 8 cm by 28 cm. Adding 4 (6 cm by 11 cm) is not an enlargement.

items.q: Triangle B is an enlargement of triangle A. What is the scale factor?
items.e: Compare matching sides: 6 ÷ 3 = 2 and 8 ÷ 4 = 2. Each side is 2 times as long, so the scale factor is 2. The difference (6 − 3 = 3) is not the scale factor.

items.q: Which rectangle is an enlargement of a rectangle 1 cm by 4 cm?
items.e: In an enlargement both sides are multiplied by the same number. 1 × 5 = 5 and 4 × 5 = 20, so 5 cm by 20 cm is an enlargement with scale factor 5.

items.q: Leo and Ruby share some stickers in the ratio 5 : 6. Leo gets 25 stickers. How many stickers were there altogether?
items.e: One part: 25 ÷ 5 = 5. There are 5 + 6 = 11 parts altogether: 11 × 5 = 55.

items.q: George and Noah share some money in the ratio 2 : 5. George gets £16. How much does Noah get?
items.e: George’s 2 parts are £16, so one part is £16 ÷ 2 = £8. Noah gets 5 parts: 5 × £8 = £40.

items.q: The ratio of Zara’s cards to Ethan’s cards is 3 : 7. Ethan has 28 more cards than Zara. How many cards does Ethan have?
items.e: Ethan has 7 − 3 = 4 more parts. Those 4 parts are 28 cards, so one part is 28 ÷ 4 = 7. Zara: 3 × 7 = 21. Ethan: 7 × 7 = 49. Answer: 49.

items.q: In a box there are 5 times as many blue pens as red pens. There are 30 pens altogether. How many red pens are there?
items.e: 5 times as many means the ratio blue pens : red pens is 5 : 1. That is 5 + 1 = 6 equal parts. One part: 30 ÷ 6 = 5. Red pens: 5.

items.q: Lily and Freya share some stickers in the ratio 7 : 4. Lily gets 21 stickers. How many stickers were there altogether?
items.e: One part: 21 ÷ 7 = 3. There are 7 + 4 = 11 parts altogether: 11 × 3 = 33.

items.q: Grace and Amelia share 35 cards in the ratio 2 : 5. How many cards does Amelia get?
items.e: There are 2 + 5 = 7 equal parts. One part is 35 ÷ 7 = 5. Amelia gets 5 parts: 5 × 5 = 25. Do not divide 35 by 5 on its own.

items.q: Aisha and Harry share £84 in the ratio 4 : 3. How much does Aisha get?
items.e: There are 4 + 3 = 7 equal parts. One part is £84 ÷ 7 = £12. Aisha gets 4 parts: 4 × £12 = £48. Do not divide £84 by 4 on its own.

items.q: In a swimming pool there are 4 times as many adults as children. There are 40 people altogether. How many adults are there?
items.e: 4 times as many means the ratio adults : children is 4 : 1. That is 4 + 1 = 5 equal parts. One part: 40 ÷ 5 = 8. Adults: 4 × 8 = 32.

items.q: A bag has 30 beads. 25 of them are red and the rest are blue. How many blue beads are there?
items.e: 25 of 30: 30 ÷ 5 = 6, and 2 × 6 = 12. The rest: 30 − 12 = 18. (Or: the rest is 35, and 3 × 6 = 18.)

items.q: In a football club there are 3 times as many boys as girls. There are 36 children altogether. How many girls are there?
items.e: 3 times as many means the ratio boys : girls is 3 : 1. That is 3 + 1 = 4 equal parts. One part: 36 ÷ 4 = 9. Girls: 9.

items.q: Leo and Ruby share £42 in the ratio 3 : 4. How much does Leo get?
items.e: There are 3 + 4 = 7 equal parts. One part is £42 ÷ 7 = £6. Leo gets 3 parts: 3 × £6 = £18. Do not divide £42 by 3 on its own.

items.q: Charlie and Evie share £90 in the ratio 4 : 5. How much does Evie get?
items.e: There are 4 + 5 = 9 equal parts. One part is £90 ÷ 9 = £10. Evie gets 5 parts: 5 × £10 = £50. Do not divide £90 by 5 on its own.

items.q: Poppy and Isla share 35 marbles in the ratio 5 : 2. How many marbles does Poppy get?
items.e: There are 5 + 2 = 7 equal parts. One part is 35 ÷ 7 = 5. Poppy gets 5 parts: 5 × 5 = 25. Do not divide 35 by 5 on its own.

items.q: A bag has 35 sweets. 47 of them are strawberry and the rest are lemon. How many lemon sweets are there?
items.e: 47 of 35: 35 ÷ 7 = 5, and 4 × 5 = 20. The rest: 35 − 20 = 15. (Or: the rest is 37, and 3 × 5 = 15.)

items.q: In a class of 32 pupils, 38 of the pupils have school dinners. The rest bring a packed lunch. How many pupils bring a packed lunch?
items.e: 38 of 32: 32 ÷ 8 = 4, and 3 × 4 = 12. The rest: 32 − 12 = 20. (Or: the rest is 58, and 5 × 4 = 20.)

items.q: The ratio of Oliver’s cards to Alfie’s cards is 3 : 5. Alfie has 8 more cards than Oliver. How many cards do they have altogether?
items.e: Alfie has 5 − 3 = 2 more parts. Those 2 parts are 8 cards, so one part is 8 ÷ 2 = 4. Oliver: 3 × 4 = 12. Alfie: 5 × 4 = 20. Answer: 32.

items.q: Kai and Mohammed share some money in the ratio 7 : 2. Kai gets £42. How much does Mohammed get?
items.e: Kai’s 7 parts are £42, so one part is £42 ÷ 7 = £6. Mohammed gets 2 parts: 2 × £6 = £12.

items.q: Jack and Maya share 30 stickers in the ratio 2 : 3. How many stickers does Maya get?
items.e: There are 2 + 3 = 5 equal parts. One part is 30 ÷ 5 = 6. Maya gets 3 parts: 3 × 6 = 18. Do not divide 30 by 3 on its own.

items.q: In a car park there are 3 times as many cars as bikes. There are 48 vehicles altogether. How many cars are there?
items.e: 3 times as many means the ratio cars : bikes is 3 : 1. That is 3 + 1 = 4 equal parts. One part: 48 ÷ 4 = 12. Cars: 3 × 12 = 36.

items.q: The ratio of Arjun’s cards to Ava’s cards is 2 : 7. Ava has 25 more cards than Arjun. How many cards does Arjun have?
items.e: Ava has 7 − 2 = 5 more parts. Those 5 parts are 25 cards, so one part is 25 ÷ 5 = 5. Arjun: 2 × 5 = 10. Ava: 7 × 5 = 35. Answer: 10.

sets.title: Ratio and proportion word problems (SATs style)

items.q: In a class of 36 pupils, the ratio of boys to girls is 4 : 5. How many more girls than boys are there?
items.e: 4 + 5 = 9 parts, so one part is 36 ÷ 9 = 4. Boys: 4 × 4 = 16. Girls: 5 × 4 = 20. 20 − 16 = 4 more girls.

items.q: On a map, 1 cm represents 5 km. A lake is 40 km from a village. How far is this on the map?
items.e: Every 5 km is 1 cm on the map. 40 ÷ 5 = 8 cm. Multiplying (40 × 5 = 200) gives a map bigger than the real distance.

items.q: Orange paint is made by mixing red paint and yellow paint in the ratio 1 : 4. A teacher makes 2 litres of orange paint. How much red paint does she use?
items.e: 2 litres = 2,000 ml. There are 1 + 4 = 5 parts, so 1 part is 2,000 ÷ 5 = 400 ml. Red is 1 part: 400 ml. Dividing by 4 (500 ml) forgets the red part.

items.q: 4 bananas cost 96p. How much do 7 bananas cost?
items.e: 1 banana costs 96p ÷ 4 = 24p. 7 bananas cost 7 × 24p = 168p = £1.68.

items.q: A bag has red beads and blue beads in the ratio 2 : 7. There are 35 more blue beads than red beads. How many red beads are there?
items.e: Blue has 7 − 2 = 5 more parts. 5 parts are 35, so one part is 7. Red is 2 parts: 2 × 7 = 14 red beads.

items.q: In a bag of sweets, for every 3 red sweets there are 4 green sweets. There are 21 red sweets. How many sweets are in the bag altogether?
items.e: 21 ÷ 3 = 7 groups. Each group has 3 + 4 = 7 sweets: 7 × 7 = 49 sweets. 28 is only the green sweets.

items.q: On a map, 1 cm represents 5 km. Two towns are 7 cm apart on the map. How far apart are they in real life?
items.e: Each centimetre stands for 5 km. 7 × 5 = 35 km. Do not add (7 + 5) or divide (7 ÷ 5).

items.q: A toy lorry is 12 cm long. The real lorry is 50 times as long. How long is the real lorry in metres?
items.e: 12 × 50 = 600 cm. There are 100 cm in 1 m, so 600 cm = 6 m.

items.q: A pancake recipe for 4 people uses 300 ml of milk. Ruby makes pancakes for 10 people. How much milk does she need?
items.e: For 1 person: 300 ÷ 4 = 75 ml. For 10 people: 75 × 10 = 750 ml.

items.q: On a map, 2 cm represents 3 km. Two villages are 10 cm apart on the map. How far apart are they in real life?
items.e: 10 cm is 10 ÷ 2 = 5 lots of 2 cm. Each lot is 3 km: 5 × 3 = 15 km. 10 + 1 = 11 km adds instead of multiplying.

items.q: Aisha and Harry share 45 sweets in the ratio 4 : 5. How many sweets does Harry get?
items.e: 4 + 5 = 9 parts. One part is 45 ÷ 9 = 5. Harry gets 5 parts: 5 × 5 = 25 sweets. 45 ÷ 5 = 9 divides by the wrong number.

items.q: Jack has 3 times as many sweets as Maya. Together they have 48 sweets. How many sweets does Jack have?
items.e: The ratio is 3 : 1, so there are 4 equal parts. One part: 48 ÷ 4 = 12. Jack has 3 × 12 = 36 sweets. 48 ÷ 3 = 16 forgets Maya’s part.

items.q: Poppy and Isla share some sweets in the ratio 3 : 5. Isla gets 12 more sweets than Poppy. How many sweets are there altogether?
items.e: Isla has 5 − 3 = 2 more parts. 2 parts are 12, so one part is 6. Altogether: 8 parts × 6 = 48 sweets. 96 uses 12 as one part.

items.q: On a map, 1 cm represents 250 m. A footpath is 6 cm long on the map. How long is the real footpath in kilometres?
In a school choir, the ratio of adults to children is 2 : 7. There are 63 people in the choir. How many children are there?
items.e: 2 + 7 = 9 parts, so one part is 63 ÷ 9 = 7. Children: 7 × 7 = 49 children. 14 is the number of adults.

items.q: 3 notebooks cost £2.40. How much do 5 notebooks cost?
items.e: 1 notebook costs £2.40 ÷ 3 = 80p. 5 notebooks cost 5 × 80p = £4.00.

items.q: Grey paint is made by mixing black paint and white paint in the ratio 1 : 5. Evie has 150 ml of black paint and uses all of it. How much grey paint can she make?
items.e: White: 5 × 150 = 750 ml. Grey paint is the black and the white together: 150 + 750 = 900 ml.

items.q: A recipe for 12 flapjacks uses 150 g of oats. How many grams of oats are needed for 18 flapjacks?
items.e: 18 is 12 + 6, and 6 is half of 12. So add half of 150 g: 150 + 75 = 225 g. (Or: 150 ÷ 12 × 18 = 225.) 156 g adds 6 instead of scaling.

items.q: A photo is 10 cm wide and 15 cm tall. It is enlarged so that it is 30 cm wide. How tall is the enlarged photo?
items.e: 30 ÷ 10 = 3, so the scale factor is 3. Height: 15 × 3 = 45 cm. 15 + 20 = 35 cm adds instead of multiplying.

items.q: To make green paint, Charlie mixes blue paint and yellow paint in the ratio 2 : 3. He uses 400 ml of blue paint. How much yellow paint does he need?
items.e: 400 ml is 2 parts, so 1 part is 400 ÷ 2 = 200 ml. Yellow is 3 parts: 3 × 200 = 600 ml. Adding 1 (401 ml) keeps the difference, not the ratio.
